judgment.rationale: A new code-grounded comment identifies the legacy matrix/setup persistence path and points to merged PR #51305. The PR diff confirms both paths now assign the stored key before the runtime key. Existing work should be verified, not replaced by another design or treated as an already shipped resolution.
evidence: The original reporter tried generated and simple manual keys, multiple entry methods, IP mapping and reinstalling; matching stopped-process settings edits work.
The October 17 update reports failure on 0.102.2862.0 with both install scopes, differing magic numbers and apparent 22-to-16-character reversion.
The October 20 comment traces UpdateKey and the setup wizard changing only the runtime key, followed by layout save and settings reload restoring the old stored key.
PR #51305 merged on 2026-10-20T03:14:25Z; its frmMatrix.cs and SetupPage2a.cs diffs add Setting.Values.MyKey assignments before Encryption.MyKey.
PR #51377 remains open and overlaps matrix-key persistence; #51080 remains open for settings I/O resilience. Neither proves that every key mismatch has the same cause.
judgment.recommended_action: Verify matrix and wizard key edits on matched-version peers using a build containing #51305; separate any remaining PowerToys Settings or I/O failure before claiming resolution.

fix_assessment.rationale: Merged PR #51305 concretely changes both legacy UI key-entry paths to persist the key before changing the runtime value. This matches the reported stopped-process workaround and new code trace. The broader PR also changes service-mode storage, so two-machine and mode-specific validation are still required. Open #51377 is overlapping work, not a reason to invent a competing fix. Merge is not proof of release availability or complete symptom coverage.

issue_context.summary: MWB rejects keys entered through the legacy UI while stopped-process settings edits connect successfully. New discussion traces stored/runtime key divergence and links a now-merged correction in #51305 covering both the matrix and setup wizard.
known_information: Original build 0.101.2362.0 was installed with WinGet; simple 16-character keys failed too, so special-character escaping alone is insufficient.
The October 17 commenter reports the same failure on 0.102.2862.0 in both per-user and machine-wide installations.
Both behavior reports say editing settings only while PowerToys/MWB is stopped restores connection.
The latest commenter explicitly limits the code explanation to the original MWB window and wizard and says no two-machine test was performed.
The issue remains open and unassigned, with five comments and no Needs-Author-Feedback label.
A maintainer requested diagnostics in August; no ZIP is attached, but later substantive reports and a concrete code trace now support direct maintainer verification.
#51305 is merged; #51377 and settings-resilience PR #51080 are still open.
inferences: A layout save followed by reload of the old key is a well-supported explanation for legacy typed-key failure, but end-to-end resolution remains untested here.
The apparent truncation to 16 characters may be the previous generated key being restored, rather than an independent input-length defect; compare actual state before proposing a truncation fix.
If the failing edit originated from PowerToys Settings rather than the legacy UI, this exact cause may not apply; logged save failures or unmatched peer versions remain separate discriminators.
The October reports from released builds do not demonstrate failure of a later merged change.
issue_context.analysis: Preserve the original careful separation of persistence, protocol compatibility and I/O failures, but replace the stale recommendation to validate only #51377 with the merged #51305 matrix-and-wizard change. Do not close the issue merely because a PR merged, ask for pairing secrets, or repeat a broad file-lock duplicate recommendation.

actions.label: Verify matrix and wizard persistence after #51305

reproduce.title: Compare legacy key-entry paths after the merged persistence correction
reproduce.version_requirement: Identical exact builds on both peers. Compare reported 0.102.2862.0 with an isolated build containing merged #51305; do not assume the merged change is already in a release.
prerequisites: Two Windows test machines with MWB enabled and a permitted network connection.
Disposable test configuration with backups; use synthetic pairing keys and never publish actual keys or full settings files.
Identify the legacy matrix form, its setup wizard and the PowerToys Settings page as separate entry surfaces.
setup: Prepare two valid synthetic keys and record the build and installation scope on each peer.
Test normal mode first, then service mode with the permissions required by #51305; do not silently change production pairing.
steps: 1. Establish a connection with a known synthetic key on matched-version peers.
2. Enter the same different valid key in the legacy matrix form on both machines; apply and observe the runtime state before and after layout save/reload.
3. Reopen the form and restart MWB to check persistence, then repeat through the original setup wizard.
4. Repeat in the matched build containing #51305 and confirm the stored key is updated before runtime use in both paths.
5. Compare accepted long-key input with the previously saved 16-character key to distinguish true truncation from old-key restoration; invalid input must not replace the working key.
6. Exercise the PowerToys Settings connection path separately and repeat normal/service-mode tests, checking any key replacement guidance required by the merged change.
7. If failures remain, classify protocol-version mismatch, settings-save failure and legacy reversion separately before selecting further work.
reproduce.expected_result: Accepted matrix and wizard key edits survive reload and restart and connect matched peers; invalid input preserves the working key. Remaining failures have an identified surface and mechanism rather than being assumed fixed or duplicate.
